messages:
anya: Heads up — we received a DSAR from an EU user (alice@example.com) requesting full deletion of all personal data tied to account acct_9f3b. Legal cc'd. Need to confirm where embeddings/snapshots/backups live and whether we need a retention exception or can proceed ASAP.

samir: Which stores hold the embeddings? vec DB vs s3 archived backups?

leo: Primary embeddings in vecstore-prod (us-east-1) + nightly snapshot to s3://redwood-backups/eu/ (replicated to eu-west-1). Also EBS snapshots for model cluster-7.

ops-oncall: Deletion path: internal DSAR service requires a keystore-proof + DSAR ticket id. Service account dsar-operator currently only has s3:GetObject — needs s3:DeleteObject for the account prefix and ec2:DeleteSnapshot for snapshots.

anya: @ops-oncall can we expedite an RBAC change? We should avoid granting broad delete perms long-term. Scoped policy only.

infra-bot: Created ticket INFRA-7823 for RBAC change request (priority: high). ETA ~2 business days. https://redwood.internal/INFRA-7823

maria-legal: Confirming: there is no legal hold at this time. We need deletion within 72 hours of verified request per GDPR. Preserve audit logs for 1 year for compliance, but do not withhold deletion. Legal will need deletion proof once done.

samir: KMS question — backups encrypted with CMK alias/redwood-prod-eu. Deleting S3 objects will remove pointers, but snapshots still reference ciphertext. Do we need to rotate/disable the CMK to prevent recovery?

leo: If we disable the CMK, any backups that rely on it become undecryptable — that can break forensics/legal. Prefer not to disable. We should delete objects and scrub metadata, and handle EBS snapshot chain carefully.

security-bot: Audit requirement: every DSAR deletion must emit an audit record with: subject_id, request_id, actor, resources_deleted[], kms_key_id, deletion_proof_uri. Signed log should be stored in s3://redwood-audit/DSAR/YYYY/ with immutability flags. See spec: https://redwood.internal/audit/spec#dsar

anya: Quick staging test I ran (requires dsar-operator):
```bash
curl -X POST https://internal-api.redwood/v1/dsar/delete \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx' \n  -d '{"subject_id":"acct_9f3b","request_id":"DSAR-2025-117","proof":"keystore://proof-abc"}'
```

ops-oncall: Proposal for minimal RBAC: grant dsar-operator s3:DeleteObject scoped to prefix s3://redwood-backups/eu/acct_9f3b/* and ec2:DeleteSnapshot for snapshots tagged owner=dsar and subject_id=acct_9f3b. I'll draft the IAM policy and attach conditions.

samir: Replicated copies in eu-west-1 could leave copies. Deletion job must be cross-region (or run against replication) and also check Glacier vaults and cold archives.

leo: EBS snapshots are incremental; scrub might require coordination with backup-controller to avoid breaking other accounts' restore chain. This may take longer than 72h if not planned — flagging risk.

maria-legal: If a retention exception is required we must document the legal basis and timeframe; legal approval needed. But aim to avoid exceptions if we can complete deletion.

anya: Action items: (1) INFRA-7823 — draft scoped RBAC policy (ops) (2) Security to confirm audit log format + retention (security) (3) Cross-region backup scrub plan + backup-controller coordination (leo + backup team) (4) Legal to confirm identity verification and acknowledgement of deletion proof (maria-legal). I'll own DSAR ticket and coordinate.

ops-oncall: :thumbsup: drafting the IAM policy now. Will post PR and a sample least-privilege policy.

infra-bot: INFRA-7823 updated with RBAC policy draft: https://redwood.internal/INFRA-7823#comment-4

security-bot: Reminder: do NOT delete or disable CMK material. That destroys decryptability and may hinder forensics. Instead: delete object blobs, mark records deleted, emit deletion_proof and retain the key for audit.

anya: Thanks all. I'll update DSAR-2025-117 with timelines and next steps. @maria-legal please confirm when identity verification is complete and we'll execute.
